links.outcome: Hallucinations and content mistakes in AI-generated discharge summaries rated by blinded specialists
links.effect: Hallucinations present in 40% of AI-DS, 37.5% deemed highly clinically relevant; minor content mistakes in 30% of AI vs 10% of human DS.
links.quote: Hallucinations were present in 40 % of AI-DS, with 37.5 % deemed highly clinically relevant.

links.outcome: Blinded specialist quality ratings of AI-generated vs resident-written discharge summaries
links.effect: Human DS rated higher than AI (mean 3.78 vs 3.12, p<0.05); humans surpassed AI in 12/15 questions and 16/20 cases; favored by 7/8 raters.
links.quote: Human-written DS were rated significantly higher than AI (mean ratings: human 3.78, AI 3.12, p < 0.05).

screen.reason: Retrospective evaluation comparing ChatGPT-4 generated psychiatric discharge summaries to resident-written summaries using expert raters, without testing a specific organizational deployment safeguard or practice intervention.
